title: Photoluminescent Escape Path Marking Strip, Initial Cabin Standard
abstract: A non-electrical escape path marking option, using photoluminescent strip bonded to the seat track cover line. Offered to operators wanting to remove the electrically powered floor marking and its periodic functional test.

sections.reason: Several operators asked for a floor proximity escape path marking that did not depend on the emergency power system, mainly to remove the periodic functional test and the battery maintenance that goes with the powered installation. Photoluminescent strip was an accepted means of compliance and was already flying on other types, so the change was raised as a customer option rather than to correct a defect. Charging performance under the cabin lighting fitted to this aircraft had to be demonstrated because the ceiling wash luminaires sit further from the floor than on earlier types.
sections.description: Photoluminescent strip is bonded along the seat track cover line on both aisles and around each exit, with a marker at every seat row. The lining panel D3320007009192 is replaced by a version with a recessed channel that protects the strip edge, and tubular spacers AES27771-7A lift the panel to keep the channel clear of the seat track. The exit panel 841LP7 receives an additional strip segment. Work is in zones 291 and 241 with seats in place and carpet lifted along the aisle line. The powered floor marking and its wiring are removed, and the emergency lighting controller is set to the option that inhibits the floor channel.
sections.effects: Mass reduction of 22 kg per aircraft, distributed along the cabin. Electrical load reduced by 340 VA in the emergency case. Not interchangeable: reverting requires the removed wiring to be reinstalled. The powered floor marking functional test is deleted. A charge time placard is added at each cabin attendant station, and the cabin crew procedure changes because the strip needs a minimum charge period after a dark turnaround.
sections.embodiment_note: Retrofit only, through Service Bulletin MRD-33-1047. Never cut into the production line: the strip is a customer option and the powered installation remains the delivery standard. Typical embodiment is a five-day cabin-out visit for four people, so operators take it at a cabin reconfiguration.

type_data.balance_impact: Distributed along the cabin, no reportable CG shift
type_data.production_impact: No production cut-in, offered as a retrofit option only

title: Photoluminescent Escape Path Marking Strip, Initial Cabin Standard

issue.reason: Marking strip added to the material list as a consumable, with the length destroyed per aircraft when the floor panel joints are opened quantified in the embodiment estimate.

abstract: A non-electrical escape path marking option, using photoluminescent strip bonded to the seat track cover line. Offered to operators wanting to remove the electrically powered floor marking; the strip is a consumable and is destroyed by any work that opens the floor panel joints it crosses.

sections.description: Photoluminescent strip is bonded along the seat track cover line on both aisles and around each exit, with a marker at every seat row. The strip and the exit marker segments are supplied under RO886925-91. The lining panel D3320007009192 is replaced by a version with a recessed channel that protects the strip edge, and tubular spacers AES27771-7A lift the panel to keep the channel clear of the seat track. The exit panel 841LP7 receives an additional strip segment. Work is in zones 291 and 241 with seats in place and carpet lifted along the aisle line. The powered floor marking and its wiring are removed, and the emergency lighting controller is set to the option that inhibits the floor channel. The strip is bonded across the floor panel joint line and cannot be lifted and refitted: once the adhesive has cured, any work that opens a panel joint destroys the length of strip that crosses it.
sections.effects: Mass reduction of 22 kg per aircraft, distributed along the cabin. Electrical load reduced by 340 VA in the emergency case. Not interchangeable: reverting requires the removed wiring to be reinstalled. The powered floor marking functional test is deleted. A charge time placard is added at each cabin attendant station, and the cabin crew procedure changes because the strip needs a minimum charge period after a dark turnaround. The strip is a consumable for every later floor intervention: opening the panel joints between stations 41 and 48 destroys about 9 m of strip per aircraft on a twin-aisle layout, and that length has to be carried in the material list of any change that lifts those panels.
sections.embodiment_note: Retrofit only, through Service Bulletin MRD-33-1047. Never cut into the production line. The embodiment estimate now carries 9 m of strip per aircraft as a consumable renewal allowance in addition to the initial installation length, so that a floor intervention planned against another modification is not costed as though the marking survived it.

title: Photoluminescent Escape Path Marking Strip, Initial Cabin Standard

issue.reason: Supersession by the diode standard tied to per-aircraft embodiment rather than to a fleet date, with the withdrawal sequence published alongside.

abstract: The original non-electrical escape path marking option, using photoluminescent strip bonded to the seat track cover line. Offered to operators wanting to remove the electrically powered floor marking; now replaced by a later standard, aircraft by aircraft.

sections.reason: Several operators asked for a floor proximity escape path marking that did not depend on the emergency power system, mainly to remove the periodic functional test and the battery maintenance that goes with the powered installation. Photoluminescent strip was an accepted means of compliance and was already flying on other types, so the change was raised as a customer option rather than to correct a defect. Charging performance under the cabin lighting fitted to this aircraft had to be demonstrated because the ceiling wash luminaires sit further from the floor than on earlier types.
sections.description: Photoluminescent strip is bonded along the seat track cover line on both aisles and around each exit, with a marker at every seat row. The lining panel D3320007009192 is replaced by a version with a recessed channel that protects the strip edge, and tubular spacers AES27771-7A lift the panel to keep the channel clear of the seat track. The exit panel 841LP7 receives an additional strip segment. Work is in zones 291 and 241 with seats in place and carpet lifted along the aisle line. The powered floor marking and its wiring are removed, and the emergency lighting controller is set to the option that inhibits the floor channel.
sections.effects: Mass reduction of 22 kg per aircraft, distributed along the cabin. Electrical load reduced by 340 VA in the emergency case. Not interchangeable: reverting requires the removed wiring to be reinstalled. The powered floor marking functional test is deleted. A charge time placard is added at each cabin attendant station, and the cabin crew procedure changes because the strip needs a minimum charge period after a dark turnaround. The strip is a consumable for every later floor intervention: opening the panel joints between stations 41 and 48 destroys about 9 m of strip per aircraft on a twin-aisle layout, and that length has to be carried in the material list of any change that lifts those panels. This standard remains the certified means of compliance with the floor proximity marking requirement on every aircraft that carries it, and it stays so until that aircraft is at the diode standard.
sections.embodiment_note: Retrofit only, through Service Bulletin MRD-33-1047, taken by four operators. Never cut into the production line. Superseded by the light-emitting diode standard of MOD-164122, which recovers most of the weight benefit without the charge time restriction. The withdrawal is per aircraft and not per fleet: this standard is withdrawn on an aircraft on the day the diode standard is recorded as embodied on it, and not before. Eleven aircraft were still at this standard when the supersession was declared, and the withdrawal sequence for them is published with this issue and repeated in the operator letter, aircraft by aircraft with the planned diode embodiment date against each. Withdrawing on a single fleet date would have left every aircraft not yet converted without a certified means of compliance.
